newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Refugee children to fly home as U.S. envoy arrives.
newsitem.headline: Refugee children to fly home as U.S. envoy arrives.

text.p: Some 150 Rwandan Hutu refugee children were due to fly home on Wednesday as a senior U.S. diplomat visits makeshift camps where thousands of refugees are gathering in dreadful conditions, aid officials said.

The children, all unaccompanied, were found wandering in sprawling Kasese and Biaro camps by aid workers on Tuesday as thousands of refugees began returning after a week-long flight to escape attacks by local villagers.
Bill Richardson, United States ambassador to the United Nations, was due in Kisangani on Wednesday for a short visit to the camps, about 41 km (25 miles) south of this city.
What he sees is likely to prompt further U.S. calls for a swift solution to both the refugee crisis and the conflict between the rebels of Laurent Kabila and the Zairean government.

On Tuesday, thousands more refugees emerged from the dense forest around the camps they fled last week after attacks by local villagers, which the refugees said were orchestrated by Zairean rebel soldiers.

They mobbed three food trucks allowed into the camp by rebel authorities. Kabila said on Sunday aid agencies would be given every assistance to meet a rebel-imposed deadline of 60 days to return all remaining refugees.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the U.N. food aid agency WFP had wanted to send at least 11 trucks loaded with supplies to replace those lost last week.
Aid officials said conditions in the camp appeared to have worsened slightly as the swell of returning refugees grew. More than 80,000 refugees had fled in panic.
Heavy rain is adding to logistical problems, while a rickety ferry -- the only link between the north and south banks of the Zaire river -- adds to problems.
Aid agencies hope to carry all the refugees by truck or train from their southern camps to the river, cross by ferry and airlift them home from one of Kisangani's two airports.
But rebel authorities told Reuters on Tuesday the train would not be allowed to carry refugees to Kisangani. No explanation was given.
The WFP is also waiting for permission to move tons of food from Kisangani to the camps.
In Luxemborg on Tuesday, European Union commissioner Emma Bonino accused rebel forces of a drive to wipe out refugees believed to have taken part in genocide in Rwanda.

"There can be little doubt that human rights abuses are being perpetrated against refugees," said Bonino, responsible for humanitarian aid. "I strongly believe that this is the result of a deliberate strategy to get rid of these people."
Kabila has rejected such charges and on Wednesday told Reuters in Lubumbashi, Zaire, he backed an independent probe.
